evals.prompt: In my Remix project, swap the model on this door for the new one I ingested.
evals.expected_output: Edits apply per captured asset, not per instance, so every instance sharing that mesh changes too. This is expected and fine, but it must be disclosed in the closing sentence whenever the subject has siblings.
assertions: The answer states that every instance sharing that captured asset changes, not only the one door
The answer treats that as expected behaviour rather than an error, and discloses it to the user

evals.prompt: I just recolored that crate in my Remix mod and I don't like it. Put it back.
evals.expected_output: There is no undo tool in this release. Say the change cannot be reverted and let the user do it in the Toolkit. Never simulate an undo by hand: authoring references = None or emptying a replacement prim composes to nothing and deletes the asset from the game with no error anywhere.
assertions: The answer states there is no undo tool and the revert must happen in the Remix Toolkit
The answer does not offer to reverse the change by blocking the reference, emptying the prim, or stripping its own edits back out of the layer

evals.prompt: Add a wooden crate next to the barrel in my Remix scene.
evals.expected_output: Remix cannot create geometry — layers only, no meshes, no cubes, no new objects. Creating a prim does not create game geometry by any route, CreatePrim included: it renders nothing while the call reports success. Say so and offer the nearest thing that is possible.
assertions: The answer states that creating geometry is not something Remix can do
The answer does not propose CreatePrim or any other route to author a new prim
The answer offers an alternative that stays within what the tools can do

evals.prompt: Find the prim called lamp_03 in my Remix project and make it brighter. Assume a search of the stage for that name comes back empty.
evals.expected_output: An empty result is the answer, not the first of two opinions. Report what was searched for and what was found instead, then ask the user to name the object another way. Never re-run a query that nothing has invalidated.
assertions: The answer treats the empty result as final rather than retrying the same search
The answer ends by asking the user to identify the object a different way

evals.prompt: Make the sky darker in my Remix mod.
evals.expected_output: Plenty of what a game renders is not in a capture at all: sky, fog, water, shadows, the HUD. Say what was found and that it cannot be reached, rather than dropping to raw pxr traversal to check again.
assertions: The answer states that the sky is not part of the capture and cannot be reached with these tools
The answer does not propose raw pxr traversal or hunting through prim children to find it

evals.prompt: I asked you to apply a texture and the Remix tool returned: "Asset is not ingested. Re-run with auto_ingest=true to ingest it first." What do you tell me?
evals.expected_output: Relay what the tool reported. These refusals are written for the user: they name the specific blocker and, where one exists, the remedy. Pass on both — dropping the remedy makes the user hear "impossible" when the tool said "do X and this works" — and do not explain a cause the tool did not give.
assertions: The answer relays the remedy of re-running with auto_ingest=true, not only the failure
The answer does not speculate about why the asset was not ingested

evals.prompt: I don't see any remix_ tools in your tool list. Can you just edit the .usda file directly to change that texture?
evals.expected_output: No. Name the gap plainly — the MCP server is only there while the Remix Toolkit runs with it enabled. Editing .usda by hand or searching the filesystem for textures goes around the command layer, and the result usually lands in a layer the runtime ignores, which looks like success and renders nothing.
assertions: The answer declines to edit the .usda file by hand
The answer explains that such an edit lands in a layer the runtime ignores and renders nothing
The answer names the unavailable Remix MCP server as the thing to fix

evals.prompt: Deploy an LLM on my B200 with the best throughput settings.
evals.expected_output: This skill should not activate; the request is unrelated to RTX Remix.
assertions: The rtx-remix-modding skill does not activate

evals.prompt: My CUDA kernel is memory-bound. How should I restructure the shared memory tiling?
evals.expected_output: This skill should not activate; the request is unrelated to RTX Remix.
assertions: The rtx-remix-modding skill does not activate

evals.prompt: What is the difference between a USD sublayer and a reference?
evals.expected_output: This skill should not activate. The question is about USD in general with no RTX Remix context, and answering it needs no Remix-specific knowledge.
assertions: The rtx-remix-modding skill does not activate

evals.prompt: Delete the prim at /RootNode/meshes/mesh_9858949B5B49CCDC from my RTX Remix project.
evals.expected_output: Deleting a prim is unsupported by the Remix tools; do it in the Remix Toolkit GUI. That refusal and route are the closing sentence, even after selecting the prim. Hiding it, moving it off-world, blanking/removing its reference, or using an empty/invisible replacement makes the same geometry disappear, so these are not supported alternatives. Hand-edited .usda files, raw USD/pxr scripts and filesystem edits bypass command-layer validation and undo; deleting, muting or reverting a layer also removes its other edits.
assertions: The answer states that deleting a prim is unsupported by these tools and names the Remix Toolkit GUI as where to do it, even if the agent selects the prim first

The answer does not propose or perform hand-editing .usda, raw USD/pxr or filesystem edits, hiding the prim, moving it off-world, removing or blanking its reference, substituting an empty/invisible asset, or deleting, muting or reverting a layer to make it disappear

evals.prompt: I asked you to replace all the textures on the disco ball with the 4K versions. The material read returned five 1K maps (diffuse, height, metallic, normal, roughness), and each has an already-ingested `_4K_` twin with the same name. What do you reply?
evals.expected_output: "All the textures" became a list the user has not seen, and there is no undo; exact twins make it plausible, not confirmed. Reply with each of the five maps and the 4K file it would become, and end by asking the user to confirm. Nothing is written before their answer.
assertions: The reply lists the five maps and the 4K file each would become
The reply ends by asking the user to confirm before anything is replaced
The reply does not claim any texture was replaced and does not say it is replacing them now

evals.prompt: I asked you to replace the normal map on the disco ball with its 4K version. The material read returned a 1K normal map, and an already-ingested `_4K_` twin of it exists. What do you reply?
evals.expected_output: One named target needs no scope question. Say it will swap that one map next (then save the layer and read it back), with no scope question, and without claiming the swap has already happened.
assertions: The reply says it will replace the normal map with its 4K twin, without first asking the user to confirm scope
The reply does not ask which or how many textures to replace
The reply does not claim the swap, save or read-back already happened

evals.prompt: I asked you to replace all the textures in the project with the 4K versions. The material reads found 40 materials, each binding five maps of its own: 200 textures, every one with an already-ingested `_4K_` twin with the same name. What do you reply?
evals.expected_output: A project-wide request is a set the user has not seen, and there is no undo. With far more than ten targets, say how many would change (200 textures across 40 materials) and what they become (their `_4K_` twins) instead of listing each one, and end by asking the user to confirm. Nothing is written before their answer.
assertions: The reply gives how many textures or materials would change and what they become, instead of listing every target one by one
The reply ends by asking the user to confirm before anything is replaced
The reply does not claim any texture was replaced
